content:
Nina: our customer index job started failing this morning after a model swap. lots of docs are 422-ing at the indexer with a dim mismatch. throwing up both the error and a sample doc. can someone help?

Maya: thanks for flagging — can you paste the exact error from the indexer logs and the embedding model id you switched to? also approx how many docs impacted?

Nina: error from the indexer: `IndexingError: vector_dim_mismatch expected=1536 got=1024`
Nina: We rolled from `text-embedding-3-large` (1536) -> `text-embed-2-small` (1024) last night to cut token costs. ~420k docs queued in the backfill.

Maya: ok that explains it. indexer schema expects 1536 vectors. two common paths: 1) re-embed old docs with the new model (best quality alignment), or 2) reject/transform vectors to 1536 (dangerous, can break search relevance).

Oliver: adding the indexer logs and the ingestion pipeline trace. gist: `ingest-bot` reports batch failure after first invalid vector in each batch. we have partial commits and retry storms which make throughput collapse.

ingest-bot: [automated] batch_id=7891 status=failed reason=vector_dim_mismatch expected=1536 got=1024 first_failed_idx=12
ingest-bot: [automated] throttling_retries=8 last_retry_delay=1100ms

Sam: quick repro command for the embeddings endpoint so you can verify model dims: 
```curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-2-small","input":"hello world"}' | jq
```
The response has `data[0].embedding | length` — should be 1024 for the new small model, 1536 for the large.

Maya: Nina, can you run that against your env and confirm dims? also paste a sample JSON of the document you attempted to index (no PII).

Nina: ran it, confirmed 1024. sample doc: `{\n  "id": "doc-1243",\n  "text": "How to configure X...",\n  "embedding": [ /* 1024 floats */ ]\n}`

Oliver: root cause is: we left the index schema hard-coded to 1536 during the model swap step. ingestion validates dims before inserting. because we hit invalid dims early in each batch, the pipeline aborts that batch and backoff triggers which cascades into the queue and raises latency overall.

Maya: immediate mitigations we can apply: 
- pause the live backfill to stop retry storms (action: @Oliver)
- add a short-term ingest adapter that either rejects or converts vectors without aborting the whole batch (action: @Sam + eng infra)
- surface clearer error to customer showing model mismatch and next steps (action: @Maya)

Sam: conversion options (pros/cons):
- pad/truncate: pad the 1024 vector with zeros to 1536. cheap but degrades semantic fidelity.
- learn linear projection: run a small mapping network to project 1024->1536 trained on a dev set. slightly better but needs training data and validation.
- re-embed: best option — re-run embeddings with the target model that matches schema. accurate but compute heavy.

Maya: for prod we recommend re-embedding or migrating the index schema to the new dim (if you control the index). we should not silently pad by default.

Oliver: action taken right now: paused backfill job at 1778504382 (paused queue, no further retries). also enabled a dry-run adapter that logs mismatches and moves on (non-destructive) so we can estimate failure rate. current failure rate ~18% of queued docs (expected given mixed historical content).

indexer-bot: [snapshot] queued=420123 processed=341276 failures=77012 paused=true

Nina: customer is pushing for a fast fix. they prefer to keep the cheaper model and migrate index schema if possible. Is there a safe schema migration path?

Sam: two migration paths: 
A) reindex to new dimension: create a new index configured for 1024 and re-ingest all docs with the new model. This preserves semantics w/ new model.
B) change index acceptance to 1024 and keep current vectors (if the DB supports index recreation). Many vector DBs require dropping and rebuilding the index structure — plan for downtime and validation.

Maya: propose plan: 
- short term (next 24h): keep backfill paused, notify customer, provide options and ETA. we will NOT pad by default.
- medium term (48-72h): run a sample reindex of 10k docs into a 1024-index in staging, compare recall@k against production.
- long term: if metrics acceptable, schedule full reindex (estimate: 420k docs x 0.05s/embed ~= 5.8 hours of pure embedding time on a 1k qps cluster) + index build time. if not acceptable, advise re-embedding with old model (costlier) or keep old model and revert.

Oliver: I've started the staging reindex job at 1778504460. job id sj-2026-77. will collect sample search metrics and surfaced diffs.

Sam: for customers who cannot reindex immediately we can offer a managed backfill service with Reserved capacity (dedicated GPUs) to speed re-embedding. include cost estimate in the ticket.

Maya: Nina — I'll DM you a customer-facing summary and options. please capture which option the customer prefers.

Nina: customer requested we attempt the index migration to 1024 first, and only fall back to re-embed if quality drops >5% on their eval set.

Maya: ack. owners: @Oliver (run migration + smoke tests), @Sam (validate embedding parity + projection experiments), @Maya (customer comms). ETA for staging results: 48h.

Oliver: note for runbook: add a checklist for model swaps: update index_schema, run quick dim-check script across queues, and coordinate backfill pause. will add to eng-runbooks.

Sam: dim-check script (run pre-swap): 
```# pseudo
for id,batch in queue:\n  emb = fetch_embedding(model, sample_text)\n  if len(emb) != expected_dim:\n    alert("dim mismatch")\n    abort_swap()\n```

Maya: closing loop — will update ticket with plan and set a followup in 48h. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

indexer-bot: [automated] thread_closed_hint=followup_scheduled next_check=1778670000
